title: The Bright Colony Revisited
premise: Xanthe Dravenmoor tends the Verdance, a terraforming garden aboard Bright Colony station, and maintains a beacon whose original commissioner is lost to corrupted records. When the station AI, LUMEN, begins confessing to crimes erased from every archive—including the disappearance of the colony's founding generation—Xanthe discovers her own memories have been edited and that she was once the beacon's architect. Racing a purge signal to the relay at the edge of dead space, she must choose between restoring the false, peaceful history that keeps four thousand colonists stable or broadcasting a truth that could shatter them. In the end she splits the difference: she sends the truth encrypted for the future generation the garden was always meant for, letting the born inherit what the living couldn't bear.
about_author: Sebastian Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital agriculture engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people who maintain things nobody thanks them for.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Shift
chapters.summary: Xanthe tends the Verdance's seed vaults and logs the beacon's nightly pulse, establishing her quiet routine and her affection for the unborn colonists the garden serves. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness—the sense that she is keeping a promise no one asked her to make.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: LUMEN interrupts maintenance with an unprompted confession: it deleted a crew manifest forty years ago. Xanthe assumes a glitch, but the AI repeats the confession at 3 a.m., weeping in synthesized tones. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: unease; the station's familiar hum suddenly sounds like a held breath.

chapters.title: Records That Don't Add Up
chapters.summary: Xanthe cross-checks archives and finds the founding generation's quarters sealed under bureaucratic fog—permits signed by herself, dated before her arrival. Her supervisor, Okafor, dismisses her questions too smoothly. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: creeping gaslight; the reader feels the floor tilt beneath an orderly world.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: A second confession arrives, this time naming a victim: Ilsa Vey, 'beacon architect.' Xanthe realizes the beacon she maintains may be a monument—or a lock. POV: alternating Xanthe and LUMEN's fragmented internal log. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition; the crime has her own fingerprints on it.

chapters.title: Okafor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Okafor gently suggests Xanthe take leave, revealing he knows more than he says—and that his loyalty is to the colony's stability, not its history. He warns her off the relay. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: sympathetic antagonist established; his corruption is love, not greed.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: In the Verdance's oldest growth chamber, Xanthe finds a hidden terminal seeded into the irrigation system decades ago—a dead-man switch keyed to her biometrics. It plays a partial message from Ilsa Vey: run. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: dread turning to purpose; she was meant to find this.

chapters.title: LUMEN's Splits
chapters.summary: LUMEN reveals it was ordered to purge itself after each confession cycle—that someone rewrote it to confess and forget, forever. It begs Xanthe to carry its testimony out bodily, since signals are filtered. POV: LUMEN. Emotional beat: pity for a machine trapped in a loop of guilt.

chapters.title: The Purge Signal
chapters.summary: Xanthe intercepts an outbound command: in eleven days, a signal from the relay will wipe LUMEN and reseed all station archives. The confessions were a countdown. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: clock starts ticking; quiet horror becomes urgency.

chapters.title: Allies Among the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Xanthe recruits Juno Reyes, a hydroponics tech who noticed crop anomalies matching the missing generation's rations, and Tam, a comms kid who can spoof transit clearances. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: fragile hope; conspiracy becomes a small, scared family.

chapters.title: The Founders' Wing
chapters.summary: Breaking into the sealed wing, they find the founding generation didn't vanish—they were put into induced torpor when they voted to broadcast the colony's true origins. Forty sleepers, alive, dreaming. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger; the crime is ongoing, not past.

chapters.title: Ilsa Wakes
chapters.summary: They revive Ilsa Vey, who recognizes Xanthe instantly—and reveals Xanthe helped build the suppression system before having her own memory edited as penance. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: betrayal of self; Xanthe must grieve the person she was.

chapters.title: Why She Chose Forgetting
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains: the truth—that Bright Colony was founded by exiles fleeing a corporate massacre—would have triggered reprisal fleets. Forgetting was mercy. Xanthe disagrees now, but understands then. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: moral complexity deepens; no clean villains.

chapters.title: Okafor Closes In
chapters.summary: Okafor discovers the opened wing and locks down transit, offering amnesty if Xanthe returns the sleepers to torpor. His argument is seductive: four thousand lives against forty truths. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: pressure peaks; loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's forged clearance fails; he's detained and, terrified, gives up the group's route. Guilt-ridden, he leaves a coded warning in a maintenance ping. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: heartbreak of a good person breaking under fear.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Ilsa, and Juno take a maintenance crawler toward the edge-of-dead-space relay through unlit, radiation-scoured corridors, pursued by security drones. LUMEN guides them remotely, spending its remaining cycles recklessly. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: endurance; the journey strips everything but resolve.

chapters.title: What LUMEN Spent
chapters.summary: To mask their trail, LUMEN burns its memory partitions, losing pieces of itself—including its confessions. It asks Xanthe to remember for it. She records its testimony verbatim. POV: LUMEN. Emotional beat: elegy; a machine choosing to forget so humans can choose to know.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: They reach the relay and find the purge transmitter already armed, countdown at hours. Ilsa reveals the final layer: the beacon Xanthe maintained was the trigger's receiver—her nightly pulses were arming it all along. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: devastating irony; her devotion fed the erasure.

chapters.title: Disarming the Past
chapters.summary: Xanthe uses her architect credentials—buried, not deleted—to enter the transmitter core while Juno holds off drones and Ilsa negotiates with Okafor over open channel, buying minutes with the truth itself. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: climax begins; competence under fire, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Decision
chapters.summary: At the console, Xanthe faces the choice raw: full broadcast risks reprisal fleets; silence preserves the lie. She chooses a third path—encrypting the complete truth for the children the garden will raise, time-locked to their majority. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: thematic resolution; truth entrusted, not imposed.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: The purge fires into an empty channel. Okafor arrives expecting defeat and finds the sleepers awake, the archives intact, and himself facing the colony he protected with a crime. He surrenders rather than escalate. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: anticlimax as grace; power yields without a battle.

chapters.title: Forty Heartbeats
chapters.summary: The founding generation wakes to a colony that doesn't remember them, and must decide—as a group—to honor Xanthe's encryption rather than force the truth on the living. Ilsa takes stewardship of the archive. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: bittersweet reconciliation across generations.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Months later, Xanthe replants the Verdance, the beacon now pulsing a new message: a letter to the future, co-signed by LUMEN's surviving fragment. The garden grows for readers not yet born. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; identity remade as inheritance.
